name: Toast
purpose: A Sonner-style stacking notification, fixed to the top-right corner, triggered imperatively (toast.success('Saved')) from anywhere — not tied to a piece of UI state the consumer renders conditionally, unlike Modal/SidePanel.
neverUseFor: A message the user must act on before continuing — use Modal instead, Toast can be missed or auto-dismiss
Form field validation errors — show them inline next to the field, not as a Toast
Anything the user needs to refer back to later — Toast auto-dismisses and doesn't persist
rationale: Toast is triggered imperatively (toast.success('Saved')) instead of rendered conditionally (ADR-011), so feedback can be raised from anywhere. Toasts stack top-right at a fixed 340px width in an aria-live='polite' region, and focus inside a toast pauses auto-dismiss — which is why it's never used for anything the user must act on. Toasts further back in the stack also soften — half of component.toast.depthBlur one step back, all of it two steps back — and sharpen when the stack spreads (transitions.dev banner stacking).

mayExtendLocally: Write the message and pick the documented tone (success, error, ...)
Raise toasts from any product event through the imperative toast API
mustEscalateToDS: Changing the position, width or stacking behavior
Using Toast for blocking decisions or form validation
Adding action buttons, custom durations or persistent toasts

anatomy.description: Fixed, top-right, portaled to document.body via createPortal (ADR-011). Rendered by the <Toast /> component, mounted once by the consuming app.
One notification. Background is always the page fill — color lives only on the icon, never the card (ADR-011), a deliberate difference from Badge's own tinted-surface convention.
A real Filled Tabler icon through the Icon component, fixed per variant — not caller-supplied like Badge's own icon prop.
An IconButton (IconX) that dismisses this toast early.

width.note: Fixed viewport/card width, not on the shared size scale — same category of per-component literal as SidePanel's width.

a11y.role: each toast-viewport region uses aria-live="polite" so screen readers announce new toasts without interrupting; toast-close is a real button with an accessible label
keyboardNav: Tab reaches each visible toast's close button
Focus inside a toast (e.g. Tab onto its close button) stops its auto-dismiss and spreads the stack — the keyboard equivalent of hovering it (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable)
notes: Triggered via the imperative `toast` object (toast.success/info/warning/danger/neutral(label, description?) — the description may also be passed Sonner-style as { description }), not props on <Toast /> itself — see ADR-011. <Toast /> is the rendered stack, mounted once; it takes almost no props of its own. Calling toast.* with no <Toast /> mounted logs a console warning (nothing would be shown).

Stacking depth (max 3 visible) and hover-to-spread use real measured pixel heights (offsetHeight), not percentage-based transforms — a percentage approach was tried and broken in the pre-implementation preview by two toasts of different heights; see ADR-011.

focus.note: focus is drawn by Button, IconButton — see their a11y.applied.focus

motion: CSS transitions/animations: neutralised by the global prefers-reduced-motion rule

properties.name: variant
properties.description: Sets the filled icon (InfoCircleFilled, CircleCheckFilled, AlertTriangleFilled, AlertHexagonFilled — added to the Icons page) and its color, toast.icon.{variant}.

properties.name: description.
properties.description: Show/hide part: the line carries its own 2px top (spacing/3xs).

figma.structure: One toast: 340px, 16px padding, 12px gap, radius/l, fill/page, shadow / xl; filled icon 24px; title 12/18 bold (no text style — bound to fontSize/s, fontWeight/bold, lineHeight/s); description Body / s / Regular; IconButton ghost s (X) to dismiss. Stacking, peek and spread are runtime motion, not modeled.

KeyboardReach.reason: keyboard focus is drawn on the close IconButton inside it (state=focus)
